about:
MicroLink Devices was founded in 2000 in Niles, Illinois, a northern suburb of Chicago. The company operates a 30,000-square-foot facility that includes a clean room and device fabrication and test laboratory.

The company designs and manufactures III-V epitaxial materials for wireless devices and high-efficiency, single- and multi-junction GaAs-based solar cells and sheets. Its proprietary epitaxial lift-off (ELO) process removes the solar cell structure from the growth substrate, yielding lightweight, flexible cells while allowing substrate reuse. MicroLink owns metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) tools for high-volume epitaxial growth, along with full fabrication and test capabilities for semiconductor devices and solar cells. It also performs contract research and development, having served as a prime federal contractor on more than thirty programs since 2003.

MicroLink's products serve the aerospace, defense, and renewable energy sectors. Its solar cells and sheets are used in unmanned aerial vehicles, spacecraft, and terrestrial solar collectors. The epitaxial materials support cellular phone and wireless device manufacturers. The company has been a prime contractor on over thirty federal programs developing solar cells, transistors, and lasers.

The company emphasizes quality control, with ISO 9001 certification and a policy of verifying customer specifications before production. Its technical staff includes recognized experts in GaAs and InP device growth and processing, supporting customers through development and production. The ELO technology, developed through federal R&D programs, differentiates its solar products by enabling lightweight, flexible cells with reduced cost through substrate reuse.
